motion.name: rack
motion.value: .9s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1): blur(16px) brightness(.9) to blur(0) brightness(1), with clip-path re-seating over the same .9s
motion.purpose: Rack focus when a theme plane comes to the front. A theme with no painting rests at blur(10px) brightness(.72) saturate(1.2) in front and blur(3px) brightness(1.1) as a slice.

motion.name: window-swap
motion.purpose: The stage window fades out, changes picture, fades in when loaded.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Background, border and transform on controls; .25s for the progress bar; .3s for the top bar turning solid; .5s for slice brightness.

motion.name: drift
motion.purpose: Planes drift at different speeds as the page scrolls, where scroll-driven animation is supported.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: The stage window rises as the page scrolls.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No rack, no drift, no lift, no transitions on planes or the window, no smooth scrolling.

narrative.overview:
The site is a multiplane animation stand. Background paintings are the large surfaces, lettering sits in front of them as if inked on a clear cel, and the app itself always appears as a floating window on the nearest plane. The ground between paintings is deep umber, warm and nearly black, so that a painting never has to compete with a neutral page: where there is no picture there is only dark, warm quiet.

Density is low on the promo pages (one idea per band, a picture beside most of them) and steady on the reading pages (docs and walkthrough), which drop the paintings below the page head and become a plain three-column reader on the same ground. Everything a visitor can press is a pill. Everything that shows the app is a rounded window with a soft, deep shadow and a hairline edge. Lamp amber is the single accent: it fills the primary action and tints a warning, and nothing else. Every small mark (underlines, dots, focus rings, progress) is cel.

The home stage is the system's one piece of theatre: one painting fills the screen, the other themes stand at the right as slanted slices of their own paintings, and choosing one racks focus to it. Other pages reuse the idea at rest: a page head or a closing band carries one painting, held back by a Well shade so the lettering reads, and a tall section opens with its painting as a clear band at full strength, with no lettering on it.
keyCharacteristics: Deep umber ground with three tonal steps (well, raised, high); no neutral grey anywhere.
Paintings are surfaces, not decoration: full-bleed, always under a Well shade where text sits on them.
Gloock for titles at regular weight, Hanken Grotesk for everything read or pressed.
Pill controls with a 1.5px translucent cel edge; selected state inverts to cel white.
One accent, lamp amber: the primary action's fill and the caution tint. Links, dots, focus rings and progress are cel.
The app is shown as a floating window, never in a device frame.
Motion is focus and drift, and all of it stops under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: A lamp-amber fill on a control means "this is the primary action here". A group of controls carries at most one. Everything else in the group is a clear cel tab.

rules.name: The Marks Are Cel Rule
rules.body: Anything small that points, counts or tracks is cel, not lamp: link underlines, step dots, the focus ring, selection, the current-section highlight, progress and range controls. If a mark is amber, it is competing with the download button.

rules.name: The Warm Dark Rule
rules.body: Every dark is umber and every light is cel. Shades over paintings are the Well colour at an alpha, never plain black over text; lines are cel white at an alpha, never grey.

rules.name: The Amber Means Caution Too Rule
rules.body: Warning surfaces (the download warning card, the docs warning callout) use the same lamp hue as an 8% tint with a 60% edge. The stylesheet's --warn is the same value as --lamp. This is a deliberate second job for the hue, the only one, and it widens the direction contract's "primary action only": the solid fill stays reserved for the action, the tint and edge mean caution. A warning never carries a lamp fill.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels, table heads, nav group names and footer column labels are sentence case at weight 600 or 700 with no added tracking. The only uppercase, letter-spaced text on the site is the wordmark in the top bar and footer (700, 0.2em).

rules.name: The One Weight Serif Rule
rules.body: Gloock is always 400. Emphasis in a title comes from size, never from a bolder or italic cut. Headings balance their line breaks (text-wrap: balance).

rules.name: The Shade Before Text Rule
rules.body: Lettering never sits directly on a painting. A linear shade in the Well colour runs from 92 to 94% at the text side to 35 to 50% at the far side (on the stage: 93%, 80% at 36%, clear by 64%, plus a foot and a head shade for the names and the top bar). A tall section does not put lettering on its painting at all: the painting is a clear band (clamp(240px, 48vh, 500px) high; clamp(180px, 34vh, 300px) under 900px) and the rows stand on Umber Ground below it. Under 980px the stage shade becomes vertical (78% to 70% to 92%). Under 900px, where lettering runs the full width, a page head and a closing scene also take an even shade (78% to 90% and 80% to 86%), and fine print on a page head steps up from Mute to Dim Cel.

rules.name: The Hairline With Every Shadow Rule
rules.body: A floating window always pairs its soft shadow with a 1px cel-white ring. The ring, not the shadow, is what separates a dark screenshot from the dark ground.

rules.name: The Rack Focus Rule
rules.body: Planes change by focus, not by sliding content: the incoming plane sharpens from a 16px blur over 0.9s on cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) while slices re-seat, and the window cross-fades (0.35s). A theme with no painting comes to rest out of focus (10px blur, dimmed to 72%) because its plane is its own app capture and the sharp copy is in the window. On scroll, planes drift at different speeds and the stage window lifts 60px where scroll-driven animation is supported. State changes on controls take 0.2s. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce all of it holds still.

dos: Do put a Well-coloured shade under any lettering that sits on a painting: heaviest on the text side. In a tall section keep lettering off the painting and show it as a clear band.
Do show the app as a floating window: 10px corners, deep soft shadow, 1px cel hairline.
Do make every pressable thing a pill with a 1.5px translucent cel edge, and show "selected" by inverting to Cel White with Umber Ground text.
Do keep one lamp-filled button per group of controls, with Lamp Ink text.
Do draw small marks in cel: link underlines (cel at 50%), step dots, the focus ring (2px Cel White, 3px offset), selection, progress.
Do caption a feature picture with the theme it is shown in.
Do set titles in Gloock 400 and everything else in Hanken Grotesk; labels in sentence case at 600.
Do separate flat content with rules (1.5px above a step or card, 1px between bands) and keep it shadowless.
Do give every motion a still state under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
donts: Don't dress the site in any one app theme. The themes appear as paintings and as captures inside windows, nothing else.
Don't put the app in a device frame (laptop, monitor, browser chrome).
Don't use a painting as a small decorative tile on a neutral page; a painting is a whole surface or it is absent.
Don't spend lamp amber on anything but the primary action's fill and a warning's tint and edge: no amber underlines, dots, focus rings, progress bars or secondary buttons.
Don't introduce a second accent hue for actions, or grey neutrals, or plain black shades over text.
Don't set uppercase, letter-spaced labels; the wordmark is the only one.
Don't box the ruled cards and steps, and don't put shadows on flat content.
